Chapter 9: Building a More Just Society—Practical Steps and Everyday Choices.
You know, the idea of creating a truly just society can seem almost impossible—like you’re standing in front of a mountain, wondering how on earth you’re supposed to move it. But here’s the thing: history shows us that real change is built from countless, tiny actions. It happens through choices made every day—in classrooms, at work, and right in our own neighborhoods.
Imagine this: there’s a new manager at work. She notices that some people always get heard, while others barely get a word in. Instead of just going along with it, she starts asking questions. Who’s missing from the table? What’s stopping certain voices from being part of the conversation?
So, she makes a few small tweaks. Maybe it’s changing how people are hired, making meetings more inclusive, or simply choosing to really listen. Over time, the whole atmosphere shifts. Suddenly, people feel safer, more appreciated, and way more likely to speak up.
See, building a just society isn’t about huge, dramatic gestures. It’s about paying attention when something feels off—and being willing to do something, even if it’s just a small thing. Maybe you speak up when a friend says something that doesn’t sit right. Or you stand by a coworker who’s been overlooked. Sometimes it’s about digging into your community’s history, or volunteering for a cause that matters to you.
And let’s be honest—real change also means looking at your own habits and beliefs. Most of us don’t wake up thinking, “I want to be unfair today.” But we all have blind spots. It takes guts to admit when you’ve missed something, to listen when someone calls out a problem, and to keep learning—even when it feels uncomfortable.
Here’s something to remember: nobody can fix everything. But everyone can do something. And when enough people start making these small changes, it adds up. Those ripples create a culture where fairness isn’t the exception—it’s just how things are done.
The work is never really finished. But every step you take makes a difference.
